data.title: SC suggests Parliament to bring amendment to section 26E of SARFAESI Act
data.description:
The Supreme Court on Thursday said Parliament should consider bringing an appropriate amendment to section 26E of the SARFAESI Act and that an explanation of the expression "all other debts" in the provision may be provided authoritatively.

Section 26E of the SARFAESI Act, 2002, gives secured creditors priority to recover their debts ahead of other debts and government dues once a security interest is registered.

A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and Ujjal Bhuyan made the suggestion while referring a legal question -- whether the "deposits" sought to be recovered under the Maharashtra Protection of Interest of Depositors (in Financial Establishments) Act would fall within the ambit of the expression "all other debts" appearing in section 26E of the SARFAESI Act -- to a three-judge bench.

 

"Although our final conclusion has been to refer the issue to a larger bench, yet we consider it apposite to suggest to Parliament to bring about an appropriate amendment to section 26E of the SARFAESI Act, whereby an explanation of the expression 'all other debts' may be provided authoritatively.

"In our considered view, this would provide much clarity and respite to the banking and financial sector from the plethora of litigation that seek to judicially eradicate the ambiguity in this regard," the bench said.

The court said it finds pertinent to place this suggestion before Parliament as any uncertainty surrounding "recovery of debts" due to secured creditors is detrimental to the interest of the public at large and an anathema to the country's financial machinery.

"We urge the Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance, to seriously consider our suggestion and bring about necessary amendments," it said.

Section 26E of the Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest (SARFAESI) Act, 2002 states, "Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, after the registration of security interest, the debts due to any secured creditor shall be paid in priority over all other debts and all revenues, taxes, cesses and other rates payable to the central government or state government or local authority." The judgment came on an appeal filed by the State Bank of India (SBI) challenging an order of the Bombay High Court.

The high court dismissed the SBI's plea against an order passed by the designated court under the Maharashtra Protection of Interest of Depositors (in Financial Establishments) Act, 1999, declining it permission to appropriate Rs 3.5 crore obtained upon the sale of a property mortgaged and securitised under the SARFAESI Act.

data.title: SC seeks census SOPs from Centre, Directorate of Census Operations
data.description:
The Supreme Court on Thursday asked the Centre and the Directorate of Census Operations to place on record the standard operating procedures governing the conduct of the census within a week. This would include the methodology and safeguards for recording and verifying caste-related information.

A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana took note of the submission made by Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Centre, that she would apprise the court of the relevant SOPs.

The bench asked the law officer to provide the details within a week.

In its order dated October 12, the bench had requested the solicitor general to place on record the census SOPs being followed. It also directed that a complete set of the paper book be provided to the advocate-on-record for the Centre and the office of the solicitor general.

 

A plea by Aakash Goel raised concerns over the methodology and safeguards for collecting and verifying caste-related information under a notification of August 14 concerning the census.

"Issue an appropriate writ, order or direction directing the Respondents to disclose and place in the public domain the methodology and safeguards governing recording and verification under Item 10 of Notification S.0.4505(E) dated 14.08.2026, including the applicable Household Schedule and relevant instructions, while preserving confidentiality of individual information," it said.

The petition sought a transparent and workable mechanism to record identifying particulars of government-issued caste certificates, wherever available, and verify their authenticity through the competent authorities.

The plea asked for disclosure of the methodology, applicable household schedule and instructions governing the collection and verification of caste particulars, while ensuring the confidentiality of individual information.

Besides, it sought a direction that caste data collected during Census 2027 should not be treated as the sole basis for formulating or revising reservation policies or determining caste-based allocation of welfare resources unless a transparent and verifiable verification protocol is put in place.

It pressed for a direction to authorities to place an affidavit before the court detailing the proposed protocol and the steps taken to implement it.

data.title: Trump's fresh tariff threats: Seafood exports in a squeeze, rice unscathed
data.description:
The latest tariff decision by the Donald Trump administration is expected to put Indian seafood exporters at a huge competitive disadvantage against key rival Ecuador in the US market, according to industry sources.
 
Industry bodies and experts are also calling for diversification into other key markets, such as Japan, China, and Vietnam. Currently, Indian seafood shipments to the US attract a 10 per cent reciprocal tariff, alongside a roughly 11.5 per cent in combined anti-dumping and countervailing duties. This takes the effective tariff burden to 21–22 per cent. In comparison, Ecuador faces an overall tariff of only about 12.5 per cent, leaving Indian exporters at an immediate disadvantage of nearly 10 percentage points.
 
“If US reciprocal tariffs on Indian goods move up to between 17 per cent and 25 per cent, the total duty on Indian seafood could climb to around 37 per cent — nearly treble Ecuador’s 12.5 per cent rate. It will definitely have an impact on us,” said Pawan Kumar G, president of the Seafood Exporters Association of India.
 
India exported 1,972,018 tonnes of seafood worth ₹73,890.46 crore ($8.46 billion) in 2025-26, an all-time high in both volume and value despite global headwinds. Frozen shrimp remained the leading product, generating ₹49,037.93 crore ($5.62 billion). It accounted for 40.19 per cent of the total export volume and 66.52 per cent of total earnings in US dollar terms. The US market accounted for over 40 per cent of India’s total seafood exports.
 
Livestock sector catches tariff bug
 
According to the Compound Livestock Feed Manufacturers Association (CLFMA), the proposed 25 per cent US tariff on Indian goods adds another layer of uncertainty for India’s export-oriented industries, including segments of the livestock and allied sectors. While the actual impact will depend on the products covered and the final tariff structure, higher duties could erode the price competitiveness of Indian products in the US market, particularly as the industry looks to expand its global footprint.
 
 For India’s animal agriculture sector, this development underscores the importance of diversifying export destinations and building greater resilience across the value chain. The ongoing India-US trade negotiations will be crucial in securing favourable market access, and we hope the government will ensure that the interests of the entire livestock sector — poultry, dairy, and aqua — are adequately safeguarded,” said Sumit Sureka, chairman, CLFMA.
 
Rice trade stays on even keel 
Meanwhile, the rice industry does not expect any major trade disruption for now from the latest tariff developments. Rice is the second-largest commodity exported by India to the US, after shrimp.
 
Reports show that Indian rice exports to the US were valued at $1.52 billion in 2024, giving the country a 27 per cent share of the US market and placing it second after Thailand (55.7 per cent).
 
According to Prem Garg, national president of the Indian Rice Exporters Federation, the proposed US tariffs are unlikely to have any major impact on India’s basmati exports. Trade is expected to continue as usual, as Indian basmati enjoys strong demand and has an established consumer base in the US. While there may be some impact on pricing, no major disruption to exports is anticipated, Garg said.
                                                                                                                                                                                         With inputs from Sanjeeb Mukherjee                                

                                                     Highs and lows

  • Current seafood tariffs to US: 10 per cent reciprocal tariff with 11.5 per cent in combined anti-dumping and countervailing duties
  • Totalling to 21–22 per cent
  • Highest value of seafood export at $8.46 billion during FY26
  • Rice second-most important commodity export after shrimp
  • Export value of $1.52 billion in 2024, 27 per cent share in the US

data.title: Financial goals, liquidity needs drive MF redemptions more than mkt falls
data.description:
Achievement of financial goals and liquidity needs are more common reasons for mutual fund (MF) redemptions than equity market volatility, according to a survey of 678 mutual fund distributors (MFDs) by Wealthy, in association with Monitor Deloitte.
 
The survey found that 45 per cent of distributors cited achievement of financial goals as a reason for client redemptions, while 40 per cent pointed to liquidity needs. Poor returns were cited by 35 per cent and market falls by 30 per cent. A shift to better investment alternatives was another reason, cited by 33 per cent of respondents.
 
"Investors whose investments are linked to specific financial goals, such as children's education, retirement or buying a home, tend to remain invested for longer periods. The fact that achieving financial goals is the most frequently cited reason for redemption (45 per cent) reinforces the importance of goal-based investing in sustaining long-term investment behaviour," the report noted.
 
 
The survey also found that 62 per cent of distributors had grown their monthly systematic investment plan (SIP) book over the previous year. While 33 per cent reported no change, only 5 per cent saw a decline. Among distributors whose SIP books grew, 45 per cent reported growth of more than 20 per cent.
 
Distributors are also stepping up efforts to retain investors during market downturns. About 52 per cent said they encouraged clients to continue or start SIPs during difficult markets, while 44 per cent increased communication with clients.
 
The report also found that distributor-led investments tend to stay invested longer. About 34.4 per cent of regular-plan SIP assets had been invested for more than five years, compared with 19.9 per cent of direct-plan SIP assets.

data.title: D2C firms eye double-digit sales growth on November 27 Black Friday
data.description:
Direct-to-consumer (D2C) brands are eyeing sales growth of 10-25 per cent this year’s “Black Friday”, which falls on November 27, as the global shopping event gains traction in India and emerges as an additional window beyond the festival season.
 
Companies are betting on rising consumer interest, demand for premium products, and increased spending across categories such as beauty, personal care, fashion and wellness.
 
The expression Black Friday is American, and its origin goes back to the 19th century, when sellers gave heavy discounts following an economic depression that started on a Friday. It is on the day after Thanksgiving, which in the United States falls on the fourth Thursday of November. 
 
Homegrown makeup and beauty startup PAC Cosmetics expects sales to grow 20-25 per cent year-on-year (Y-o-Y) over last year’s Black Friday sales.
 
Wellness startup VAHDAM India expects its daily sales to increase around 50 per cent Y-o-Y. Beauty and wellness startup Wildflower Naturals is projecting a 10-15 per cent increase while skincare firm O3+ Professional anticipates a 35-40 per cent spike over regular business days.
 
For D2C brands, Black Friday is increasingly becoming more than a discount-led exercise, offering an opportunity to acquire customers, improve product discovery, and encourage higher spending.
 
Radhika Dang Gambhir, founder of Wildflower Naturals, which is introducing a dedicated Black Friday sale for the first time this year, said: “First-time buyers may be more inclined to experiment with new brands during promotional periods.”
 
The company is offering a site-wide discount of 33 per cent from November 27 to 29, with skin care, personal care and wellness products expected to drive sales.
 
Bonish Jain, founder and director, PAC Cosmetics, said: “We view Black Friday as an opportunity to encourage product discovery, make our range more accessible, and introduce more consumers to the brand.”
 
Select products from the brand are available at discounts of up to 40 per cent on Nykaa, along with bundle offers and freebies. O3+ Professional is using the event to strengthen its presence across online marketplaces such as Nykaa and Amazon.
 
“Black Friday is an important opportunity to connect with consumers through attractive offers, digital campaigns and greater product visibility,” said Vidur Kapur, director of O3+ Professional. The brand is offering a minimum 10 per cent discount and a complimentary gift on purchases of 1,999 and above.
 
For some brands, Black Friday is emerging as a more relevant sales event than the pre-Diwali shopping period.
 
“In the runup to Diwali, people think about what to buy for family and friends. After the festivities, they start thinking about their own wellbeing and the daily routines they want to get back to … that makes Black Friday a more valuable time for us than the pre-Diwali period,” said Bala Sarda, founder and chief executive officer (CEO), VAHDAM India.
 
Chirag Taneja, cofounder and CEO of ecommerce (ecom) enablement platform GoKwik, agreed. “Black Friday appeals to shoppers across faiths and communities.”
 
Last year, the four days from Black Friday to Cyber Monday generated more than 250 crore in gross merchandise value (GMV) on the GoKwik network. Daily orders during the period were 30 per cent higher than in the preceding 30 days. The company expects to exceed last year’s GMV this year.
 
Beauty and personal care accounted for 760,000 of the 1.94 million orders on the GoKwik network during last year’s Black Friday sale.
 
Amazon India said customers across Bharat were increasingly looking to upgrade to premium products, including Android smartphones priced above 30,000, side-by-side refrigerators, high-capacity front-load washing machines and energy-efficient ACs.
 
Qcom platform Instamart is also extending its offers to big-ticket categories such as smartphones, laptops, electronics and appliances, alongside everyday essentials and wellness products.

data.title: Veruschka, iconic 'Blow-Up' model and fashion artist, dies in Berlin at 87
data.description:
Vera von Lehndorff, who as Veruschka, one of the world’s first supermodels, blurred the lines between fashion and art and, in the process, became a pop-culture icon of the Swinging Sixties far beyond the confines of the runway and magazine spreads, died on Tuesday in Berlin. She was 87. Her death was announced on the website of Gräfin von Lehndorff, a clothing company owned by her sister Catharina Kappelhoff-Wulff.
 
For more than a decade, the German-born Veruschka was the stunning standard-bearer for a rapidly changing cosmopolitan culture, defined by bright colours, strong women and the collapsing barriers between high art and pop sensibilities. At 6-foot-1 and just 125 pounds, she literally stood above the crowd, even when she was wrapping her body in complex athletic poses, draped in diaphanous shifts and gowns for star photographers like Richard Avedon, Irving Penn and Helmut Newton. At one point, she was said to be the highest-paid model in the world, commanding $10,000 a day.
 
 
“There are imitations of Sophia Loren, only not as good,” Avedon once said, “and a new Garbo is discovered every decade, but there is and will always be only one Veruschka.”
 
More than just a muse, Veruschka was a collaborator, often going directly to Diana Vreeland, the powerful editor of Vogue in the 1960s, with detailed suggestions for photo shoots.
 
“I could call her up and say, ‘Diana, I have an idea,’ and she would listen to it, and if she liked it she would say, ‘Great! Let’s do it,’” Veruschka said in a 2000 interview with Dutch, a fashion magazine.
 
She considered herself an artist and saw modeling as an extension of her creative vision. “I transform myself,” she told The New York Times in 1996. “My body is my instrument and with that I work.”
 
That same year, she had a brief but memorable role in the hit film “Blow-Up,” directed by Michelangelo Antonioni. She played herself, posing suggestively for a photo session with a swinging London fashion photographer (David Hemmings) that ends with him, camera clicking away, bestride her as she writhes on the floor — an instantly iconic image that became the centerpiece of the film’s poster. By one count, she appeared on some 800 magazine covers. But she was most closely associated with Vogue and Vreeland. She was on the cover of American Vogue 13 times in 10 years, and in hundreds of photos inside its pages.
 
Many of her shoots pushed the boundaries of what fashion could be. In one shoot, she posed naked in body paint; in another, at the Grand Canyon, she wore outfits pieced together from wires. The artist Salvador Dalí covered her in shaving cream to create a “living sculpture.”
 
While living in Florence, she was approached at the Uffizi Gallery by the photographer Ugo Mulas, who suggested that she consider becoming a model. Through his connections, she was soon in front of cameras in Paris and New York, but said that she felt self-conscious about her height and size-11 feet. Eventually, she returned to Italy, where she began a relationship with the photographer Franco Rubartelli. Together, they worked on developing her modeling skills — above all, how to use her height to her advantage by contorting and extending her limbs. By 1964, she was in high demand on both sides of the Atlantic. She worked closely with Vogue and with a small number of photographers, but resisted signing long-term contracts, for fear of losing her artistic independence.
 
Even at the height of her fame, Veruschka said she was ambivalent about modeling; she found it boring, grueling and invasive. After leaving modeling, Veruschka returned to her career as an artist. She also acted occasionally, in art-house films like “Dorian Gray in the Mirror of the Yellow Press” (1984). She also had a cameo role in the 2006 James Bond film “Casino Royale”.

data.title: SP promises 25 lakh govt jobs, Rs 40,000 pension for elderly women in UP
data.description:
Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav on Thursday promised 25 lakh government jobs and employment opportunities for two to three crore youngsters over five years, an annual pension of Rs 40,000 for elderly women and a farm-loan waiver if his party comes to power in Uttar Pradesh after the 2027 Assembly polls.
 Free laptops will be distributed to students completing Class 12, Yadav announced, building on what was his government's popular scheme during the SP's tenure in Uttar Pradesh from 2012 to 2017.
 Unveiling the party's manifesto along with senior SP leaders here, Yadav said, "Our resolve is to give government jobs to 25 lakh youngsters and employment in other sectors to two to three crore young people in five years."
 
 Promising financial assistance to vulnerable sections of the society, he said elderly women would receive Rs 40,000 annually as pension and the amount would be directly transferred to their bank accounts. Labourers, women workers and artisans would also be given an annual pension of Rs 40,000, the former Uttar Pradesh chief minister said.
 "Samajwadi canteens will be opened for PDA (backward, Dalits and minorities) women and the poor, where meals will be available for Rs 5," he said.
 Yadav also promised an immediate farm loan waiver and said a corpus fund of Rs 15,000 crore would be created to ensure that sugarcane growers receive their payments within 24 hours.
 On employment and education, he announced an Urban Employment Guarantee Act for young people in cities and residential hostels for students in major urban centres.
 "We will bring back the laptop-distribution scheme for students passing the Class-12 exam," he said, adding that a state education policy would be introduced to ensure equal access to quality education.
 The SP government would also reopen 26,000 primary schools allegedly shut by the current Bharatiya Janata Party-led regime in Uttar Pradesh, he said.
 On government recruitment, Yadav promised a time-bound and transparent process, backed by an annual calendar of vacancies and examinations.
 "For vacancies requiring a single examination, the entire recruitment process will be completed within three months. For vacancies involving more than one examination, the process will be completed within six months," he said.
 Yadav also promised a corruption-free recruitment system to prevent question paper leaks, adding that officials and ministers would be held personally accountable for any lapses. The results would be declared on time and transparently, and no irregularities would be tolerated, he said.
 On social justice, Yadav said his party would get a caste census conducted in Uttar Pradesh to assess the economic and social conditions of different communities, and formulate welfare schemes accordingly.
 He promised 50 per cent reservation for Dalits and PDA communities in government contracts worth up to Rs 50 crore. A Dalit Development Council would also be constituted under the chief minister's chairmanship, he announced.
 "We will follow a zero-tolerance policy towards heinous crimes against Dalits, backward classes, minorities, Muslims, women and children. We will not allow anyone to be insulted or harassed," Yadav said.
 For senior citizens, the SP chief promised a Senior Citizens' Maintenance and Welfare Act, along with old-age homes and clubs to provide facilities and support.
 On the agricultural front, he said, "We will ensure a legal guarantee to the minimum support price for all 23 crops and milk in Uttar Pradesh."
 A price-compensation mechanism would be developed for potatoes, tomatoes, onions and other crops not covered under the MSP system, he added.
 The SP would also ensure annual increases in sugarcane prices based on the actual cost of cultivation, Yadav said.
For rural development, he announced an allocation of Rs 1.5 lakh crore for infrastructure and said new village clusters would be developed with essential facilities and internet connectivity to ensure planned growth

data.title: Prospecting for a revival: Goa gears up for 5th round of iron ore auctions
data.description:
Goa’s mining department is readying for the fifth round of iron ore block auctions in December in yet another push to revive the sector, which had ground to a standstill after a Supreme Court order banned the renewal of leases in 2012.
 
The state is lining up four to six blocks for bids next month, according to government sources. Of the 18 blocks auctioned so far since FY22, only six have managed to start operations, with a capacity of around 5 million tonnes (mt).
 
However, it has not been an easy road for the mining industry. On October 5, 2012, the Supreme Court ordered the suspension of mining activities and mineral transportation in Goa, following the Justice MB Shah Commission report on illegal mining in the state. The court later lifted the ban in April 2014, but placed an annual production cap of 20 mt.
 
Consequently, there was a fall in the sector’s contribution to the state’s non-tax revenue, declining from 46 per cent in 2010-11 to less than 4 per cent in the 2025-26 Budget estimates.
 
Mining and quarrying, which contributed 16.33 per cent of Goa’s gross state domestic product (GSDP) in 2011-12, when the sector was at its pre-shutdown peak, now accounts for less than 1 per cent. The latest figures show the sector’s share at 0.61 per cent in 2024-25.
 
 
 
With this latest thrust, the state is looking to net revenues of around ₹1,000 crore annually, which officials say is a very conservative estimate.
 
If all blocks resume operations, the total revenue could be around ₹4,000 crore annually, according to industry experts.
 
“Achieving the capacity of 20 mt should not be difficult as the 17 blocks alone have a capacity of 19 mt. We have been working closely with other departments, including forest and environment, to facilitate faster clearances for the leaseholders,” said Narayan Gad, director, Directorate of Mines and Geology in Goa.
 
The state government is also planning to approach the Supreme Court to seek permission to increase production beyond the current limit.
 
Additionally, Goa is looking to auction around 700 mt of low-grade coal lying in the dumps. After the Indian Bureau of Mines allowed the sale of these resources in a notification dated April 1, the state conducted an e-auction of 20 dumps in August and allotted eight to previous leaseholders who owned the dumps. It is also auctioning around 24 mt of processed iron ore that could not be sold after the Supreme Court ban.
 
However, some concerns remain. The delay in starting mining operations is due to a variety of factors, but primarily environmental concerns among locals and pending forest clearances.
 
A senior industry official said that, while allocating blocks, the government did not take into account that several of them are in forested areas, often on private land. Private forest land may be privately owned but qualifies as forest due to its natural vegetation.
 
On the employment side, while the mining department has put a condition that all leaseholders must provide local employment, it has not prescribed any minimum limit. The main beneficiaries are truckers. But, with full-scale operations yet to start, there is a lot of idle capacity.
 
“The revival is progressively generating business for the local transportation and ancillary sectors, although the benefits remain uneven. Truck availability presently far exceeds the demand generated by current production levels,” said Glenn Kalavampara, executive director, Western India Mineral Association.
 
The high premiums committed by bidders in the auctions have also raised questions about long-term viability. To expedite operations, the mining department has offered lower premium payments for five years from the time operations start.
 
Overcoming local resistance to mining operations is easier said than done. Goa Foundation, the state’s environmental action group that has been involved in several litigations, has already challenged three leases granted in the village of Sirigao.
 
“Past problems created by mine leaseholders are not being resolved… Fields outside the mines are getting polluted and there is no accountability,” said Rahul Das, research director, Goa Foundation.
 
As Goa prepares to expand mining, the challenge will be to get more blocks operational while addressing local opposition and environmental concerns. Chief Minister Pramod Sawant has urged residents of mining areas to cooperate, while warning mine operators of penalties for violations.

data.title: Trump seeks to keep leverage over Xi with 40% China tariff threat
data.description:
China vowed to defend its interests after the US unveiled new tariffs on Chinese goods and warned the rate could double if trade talks collapse, injecting fresh tension ahead of a planned meeting between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping.
 While the new 20% levy remains within the bounds of a trade truce set to expire in January, the threat of a 40% rate - which would kick in if trade talks break down - gives Washington leverage heading into next month's Group of 20 summit, where the two leaders are expected to meet for the fourth time this year. 
 The US announced the new tariffs on China and other trading partners Wednesday following months of investigations over excess manufacturing capacity. The tariffs are still subject to public comment and could change.
 
 "Partners have been waiting for this shoe to drop for some time," said Wendy Cutler, senior vice president at the Asia Society Policy Institute and former Acting Deputy US Trade Representative, adding that the US is using the prospect of higher tariffs as "leverage to secure expected shipments of critical minerals and rare earths, and further purchases of US agricultural goods."
 The new duties mark the latest effort by the Trump administration to restore its expansive tariff agenda after the US Supreme Court struck down earlier levies on goods from China and dozens of other economies. The proposal would put China's average effective tariff rate at about 31%, near the level before the ruling, according to Bloomberg Economics estimates. 
 While bilateral ties are likely to remain stable if the duties stay in the 20% range - a level China has previously indicated it would accept - the 40% threat will color how Beijing responds to US chip curbs and other frictions in the coming weeks as both sides negotiate an extension of the truce. Any miscalculation could quickly complicate talks, particularly with a more hawkish US Congress pressing for tougher export controls on Beijing.
 The US hasn't spelled out exactly what it would take to trigger the more drastic hike on China. A US official, speaking on condition of anonymity ahead of Wednesday's announcement, said the higher rate could kick in if Beijing doesn't comply with a trade deal reached last year. 
 At a regular briefing Thursday, Chinese Commerce Ministry spokesperson He Yadong called the US Section 301 investigation that led to the new tariffs "a quintessential act of unilateralism" and urged the two sides to use dialogue to resolve their differences. 
 Beijing "reserves the right to take necessary measures to resolutely defend its legitimate rights and interests," He added. 
In July, the Office of the US Trade Representative announced 12.5% duties on China following a Section 301 investigation into the alleged failure of around 60 economies to prevent forced labor in their supply chains. Tariffs levied under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 are generally seen as more legally durable and flexible than other tools Trump has considered, but they take longer to implement. 
 "The rate of 20% should be seen as a cap on the two Section 301 investigations," said Deborah Elms, head of trade policy at the Hinrich Foundation in Singapore. "This gives USTR more flexibility to adjust, which is especially useful when there might be a court ruling on forced labor which could ask for changed rates."
 Businesses and US states are challenging tariffs over forced labor concerns in court, accusing Trump and US officials of unlawfully using Section 301 to replace earlier tariffs that were either struck down by the US Supreme Court or expired.
 The new tariff announcement comes just a week after Trump and Xi met at a gathering of Asia-Pacific economies in Shenzhen. Both leaders appeared to lean heavily on their personal rapport to keep ties between their countries on an even keel, though new strains have emerged surrounding the alleged spy scandal involving Nvidia Corp. CEO Jensen Huang, as well as fresh US curbs on offshore chip access for Chinese companies.

data.title: Up 25.3% in a month, HDFC Bank regains No.2 spot by market capitalisation
data.description:
A month into Anup Bagchi’s tenure as managing director (MD) and chief executive officer (CEO), HDFC Bank has staged a sharp stock market comeback, with its share price surging 25.3 per cent to reclaim the second spot in the market capitalisation (mcap) rankings, overtaking Bharti Airtel. The rally marks the bank’s best monthly stock performance since 2009. 
HDFC Bank’s share price hit an eight-month high of ₹871.25, rallying 3.23 per cent on the BSE in Thursday’s intraday trade before closing at ₹866.75, up 2.7 per cent, amid heavy volumes and continued buying by foreign portfolio investors (FPIs).
The largest private-sector bank’s stock not only outper­formed the broader indices but also its peers and the Nifty Bank index on Thursday, as well as the past month. 
Over a month, HDFC Bank’s mcap has increased from ₹10.66 trillion to ₹13.38 trillion. Consequently, HDFC Bank stood second in the rankings, overtaking Airtel which closed the day with an mcap of ₹13.05 trillion, BSE data showed. Reliance Industries, with an ₹18.9 trillion mcap, stayed on top. 
Bagchi, who was with the ICICI group for 34 years, is the first outsider to become CEO of HDFC Bank, succeeding Sashidhar Jagdishan. Before taking up his current role, Bagchi was MD and CEO of ICICI Prudential Life Insurance. He also served as executive director of ICICI Bank from 2017 to 2023, overseeing retail, business and rural banking, as well as wholesale banking. 
“A confluence of factors has worked in favour of HDFC Bank’s stock over the past month,” said Arijit Malakar, equity research analyst at Ashika Stock Broking. 
 
“Concerns around leadership and management continuity have eased, while the bank’s underlying fundamentals remain strong, supported by healthy loan book and deposit growth,” he added.
 
The stock was trading at its highest level since March 6. It has surged 30 per cent from its 52-week low of ₹668.9, touched on October 28. The stock had hit a 52-week high of ₹1,017.9 on December 1, 2025.
 
“Data indicates that foreign investors have been aggressively buying financial stocks over the past few days, reversing the trend of heavy selling seen in previous months. HDFC Bank stands to be a major beneficiary of these inflows. The stock was also trading at attractive valuations at the beginning of the month, adding to its appeal. We believe there is still room for further upside and remain bullish on the stock,” Malakar added.
 
So far in November, FPIs have made net investments of ₹1.42 trillion in Indian equities, National Securities Depository data showed.
 
According to Sameer Sawant, senior research analyst — BFSI (banking, financial services and insurance) at Mirae Asset Sharekhan, public-sector bank stocks also rose sharply, primarily because FPI flows rebounded towards stocks that were relatively attractively valued. HDFC Bank was among them when compared with its peers.
 
Sawant said the overall 2026-27 second-quarter (July-September/Q2) results were healthy and that the foreign currency non-resident deposits mobilised by banks had helped lenders such as HDFC Bank maintain a healthy run rate after underperforming for several quarters. The bank’s net interest margins (NIMs), which had contracted following the HDFC merger, also contributed to the positive momentum.
 
“From here on, in the medium term, we should see an improvement in NIMs as well,” Sawant said.
 
The turnaround in HDFC Bank’s stock comes after a prolonged period of underperformance, largely following its merger with erstwhile mortgage financier HDFC Ltd in July 2023. The merger weighed on margins and slowed growth.
 
During the Q2 earnings announcement, Bagchi said the post-merger balance sheet and the broader transformation were still works in progress, but he believed much of that journey was behind the bank. “There is still work to be done,” he had said.
